messages:
Kai Morales: Quick thread: contrast + legend affordances for metric heatlines. Current legend uses subtle gray separators and thin text; on low-contrast screens its hard to parse which series is active. Proposal: add a high-contrast active state (bold label + 2px left accent) and an optional patterned swatch toggle for map/heat visuals.

Anya Gupta: Agree. Also suggest increasing touch targets in the legend to 44px min for mobile. For keyboard focus, show clear focus ring and announce \"Selected series: <name>\".

Rory Bennett: Patterned swatches are nice for colorblind users but could conflict with line overlays. Maybe pattern only for filled areas/heatmaps, keep lines as stronger color + thicker stroke for active.

Iris Alvarez: Microcopy: when toggling patterns, tooltip text = \"Accessibility patterns: show textures for colorblind-friendly view\". For the active accent copy: \"Selected\" as aria-pressed state.

Kai Morales: Outlier policy idea: show an overflow row at bottom of legend that reads \"Overflow >= X\" with count, click expands to list top 10 outliers with mini-sparkline. Keeps main scale interpretable.

Anya Gupta: On smoothing: propose default view = adaptive smoothing (more smoothing at longer time windows) + small chip in legend that reads \"Smoothed\" when active. Users can toggle to \"Raw\" which overlays raw markers.

Rory Bennett: Implementation note: when overlaying raw markers on smoothed lines, use a lighter alpha for raw points and ensure they are included in SR order. Also avoid rendering thousands of DOM nodes; use canvas or aggregated markers.

Iris Alvarez: A11y: ensure legend items have aria-describedby linking to a hidden element explaining what patterns and smoothing mean. Example SR copy: \"Smoothed lines show trend; raw markers show individual events\".

Designbot: Pushed figma: https://www.figma.com/file/new123/legend-contrast-patterns frame: legend/contrast-patterns-v1 :sparkles:

Kai Morales: Action items: Rory - prototype canvas markers and overflow list behavior. Anya - write focus and mobile touch spec. Iris - draft SR copy and tooltip microcopy. Will reconvene after mock updates.
